text.p: Ingersoll-Rand Co., the diversified industrial equipment and components manufacturer, Thursday reported modestly higher first quarter profits.
Ingersoll-Rand recently has sold off several product lines and acquired "high potential" businesses.

"With healthy markets for our products and a company-wide focus on improving all of our business processes, Ingersoll-Rand has a great potential to accelerate its earnings growth," the company said in a statement.

Ingersoll-Rand had first quarter earnings of $77.8 million, or 72 cents a share, compared with $74.5 million, or 70 cents a share a year earlier. Sales rose to $1.64 billion from $1.60 billion a year earlier.
It said total bookings for the first quarter were $1.8 billion, which, excluding discontinued businesses, represented an overall increase of slightly over 5 percent.
Bookings in the United States were up over 6 percent, and international orders were up 3 percent over last year, despite an unfavourable currency impact of about 4 percent, Ingersoll-Rand said.
Woodcliff Lake, N.J.-based Ingersoll-Rand stock was up 25 cents at $48 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
